rows.en: Recently, at gapyear.com, we conducted a survey asking HR professionals whether a gap year makes a job applicant more employable. 63% agreed that a constructive gap year, either just a few months or a year sharp spent volunteering or gaining work experience overseas, makes a job application stand out, so the evidence is there.
rows.zh: 最近，gapyear.com对人力资源专业人士开展了一项调查，询问间隔年是否会让求职者更具就业竞争力。63%的受访者表示，一段有意义的间隔年经历，无论是几个月还是一年，用来参加志愿活动或积累海外工作经验，都能使求职申请脱颖而出；这就是依据。

rows.en: As Paul Bohannan, who is a renowned anthropologist, pointed out a number of years ago, “Each science that deals with people has its own definitions of human.
rows.zh: 正如著名人类学家保罗·博汉南多年前指出的：“每一门研究人的科学，对人都有自己的定义。

rows.en: To paraphrase Barbara Miller’s statement in her textbook, Cultural Anthropology, the popular impression of anthropology is based mainly on movies and television shows that depict anthropologists as adventurers and heroes.
rows.zh: 用芭芭拉·米勒在其教科书《文化人类学》中的话来说，大众对人类学的印象主要来自电影和电视节目，这些作品把人类学家描绘成冒险家和英雄。

rows.en: Well, some do have adventures and discover treasures in Egyptian tombs and elsewhere, but mostly, their work is less glamorous and involves rather repetitive and tedious activities.
rows.zh: 有些人确实会经历冒险，在埃及陵墓等地方发现珍宝；但大多数时候，他们的工作并没有那么光鲜，而是涉及相当重复、乏味的活动。

rows.en: After the onset of the Age of Exploration, which included the discovery of the Americas, as well as travel to other distant places, the study of non-Western people began in earnest.
rows.zh: 地理大发现时代开始后，随着美洲被发现以及人们前往其他遥远的地方，对非西方民族的研究才真正展开。

rows.en: Most cultural anthropologists would limit themselves to a few geographic areas, for example, Margaret Mead in Samoa and New Guinea, and Clyde Kluckhohn with the Navajo Indians in the Southwestern United States.
rows.zh: 大多数文化人类学家把研究范围限定在几个地区，例如研究萨摩亚和新几内亚的玛格丽特·米德，以及研究美国西南部纳瓦霍印第安人的克莱德·克拉克洪。

rows.en: It is the study of different cultures through material sources, through historical objects that still remain today, rather than direct interviews or observations of the group under study.
rows.zh: 考古学通过物质资料，也就是留存至今的历史器物，研究不同文化，而不是直接访谈或观察所研究的群体。

rows.en: And ethnography, a subfield of cultural anthropology, is on the whole the systematic description of human societies, mostly based on gathering the firsthand information about something in a real natural environment, rather than in a place of study, such as a laboratory or classroom.
rows.zh: 民族志是文化人类学的一个分支，总体上是对人类社会的系统描述；它主要在真实的自然环境中收集关于某事物的第一手资料，而不是在实验室或教室等研究场所中进行。

rows.en: And it is important to note that there are several universal features common among all societies; for example, the basic similarities in human biology and the existence of two sexes.
rows.zh: 需要指出，所有社会都有一些普遍特征，例如人类生物学上的基本相似性，以及两种性别的存在。

rows.en: But for the past several decades, large numbers of “anthro” graduates have been employed in other fields, such as urban planning and administration, health care and international development.
rows.zh: 但在过去几十年中，大量人类学专业毕业生受雇于其他领域，例如城市规划与管理、医疗保健和国际发展。

rows.en: What’s more important is that although anthropologists have taken up the task of recording the processes and changes of cultures past and present, they also provide the necessary insights into where the human species is heading.
rows.zh: 更重要的是，人类学家在承担记录过去和当下文化发展过程及变化这一任务的同时，也为我们理解人类这个物种将走向何方，提供了必要的洞见。

rows.en: Today we are having Harriet Sanford on our program to hear about her career in education and her current work supporting public teachers and students through the NEA foundation.
rows.zh: 今天，我们邀请到哈丽雅特·桑福德，听她谈谈自己的教育生涯，以及她目前通过NEA基金会支持公立学校教师和学生的工作。

rows.en: Neither my mother nor father completed their education, but they were adamant that their children take advantage of all of the opportunities that a public education offers both in and out of school time.
rows.zh: 我父母都没有完成学业，但他们坚持要自己的孩子利用公共教育在课内外提供的一切机会。

rows.en: Yeah. OK. The partnership currently supports NEA school districts across the country, providing free access to EverFi’s digital resources and accompanying professional development.
rows.zh: 可以。好的。目前，这项合作为全国各地的NEA学区提供支持，让它们免费使用EverFi的数字资源，并获得配套的专业发展培训。

rows.en: I understand one of the most serious problems is that of light escaping up into the skies above our cities, and the result is we cannot see all the stars that were once visible.
rows.zh: 据我了解，最严重的问题之一是光线逸散到城市上方的天空，结果使我们无法再看见曾经可见的所有星星。

rows.en: Besides, much of the lighting which is badly designed creates very strong light and shadow contrasts, which actually creates good hiding places for criminals.
rows.zh: 而且，许多设计不当的照明会造成强烈的明暗对比，反而为犯罪分子提供很好的藏身之处。

rows.en: That way, we avoid the problem of what is called light trespass, where light escapes from the area, for example, a parking lot, that it is supposed to illuminate and goes, for instance, into nearby windows or roads.
rows.zh: 这样就能避免所谓的“光侵扰”：光线从本应照亮的区域，比如停车场，逸散出去，并照向附近的窗户或道路等地方。

rows.en: For example, if you use lighting, be it security lighting or lighting for your barbecue in the garden, just make sure it is well directed, by which I mean angled downward, and the light source itself, the bulb I mean, has a good cover on it.
rows.zh: 例如，使用照明时，无论是安保灯，还是花园烧烤用灯，都要确保照射方向合适，也就是向下照；光源本身，我指的是灯泡，也要配有合适的灯罩。

rows.en: Before we call it a day, I'd like to walk you through a famous quote from Francis Bacon: “Some books are to be tasted, others swallowed, and some few to be chewed and digested.”
rows.zh: 结束之前，我想带大家细读弗朗西斯·培根的一句名言：“书有可浅尝者，有可吞食者，少数则须咀嚼消化。”

rows.en: So, whether you’re currently deciding whether a gap year is for you, or you’re just feeling itchy to decide what to do with it, you are welcome to join us. Well, Jim.
rows.zh: 无论你正在考虑自己是否适合间隔年，还是已经迫不及待地想决定如何度过间隔年，都欢迎加入我们。那么，吉姆。

rows.en: Yes, they really do. If you’re studying veterinary science and you volunteer on a wildlife conservation project, then that can really boost your CV and experience levels by doing so.
rows.zh: 会的，他们确实很在意。如果你学兽医学，又参加了野生动物保护项目的志愿工作，这样的经历就能实实在在地为简历加分、丰富你的经验。

rows.en: Ah... on my travel list, number one, cage diving with great white sharks; number two, hitchhiking across America from New York to San Francisco; number three, touring overland in Africa, and number four is climbing Mount Qomolangma, which, let’s be honest, I need to think twice.
rows.zh: 我的旅行清单上，第一项是在防护笼里潜水，近距离接触大白鲨；第二项是搭便车横穿美国，从纽约到旧金山；第三项是在非洲进行陆路旅行；第四项是攀登珠穆朗玛峰，不过说实话，这一项我得三思。

rows.en: Well, firstly, I grew up in an international household with a German mother and an Italian-American father, so our daily lives and conversations always were more global in a lot of ways.
rows.zh: 首先，我在一个国际化家庭里长大，母亲是德国人，父亲是意大利裔美国人，因此我们的日常生活和交谈，在很多方面都更具全球视野。

rows.en: Secondly, when I was 16, I left home to go to the United World College, which is a two-year boarding school with students from 90 different countries.
rows.zh: 其次，16岁时，我离家去了世界联合学院；那是一所学制两年的寄宿学校，学生来自90个不同国家。

rows.en: There, I really grew to see the entire world as an interconnected place, and began to think of myself less with national identities and more through global and human lenses.
rows.zh: 在那里，我真正开始把整个世界看成相互联系的整体；我不再主要以国籍来定位自己，而是更多地从全球和人类整体的视角看待自己。

rows.en: In a new study published last week in the journal Nature, more than 80 scientists from multiple countries used satellite data to examine the Antarctica’s vast ice sheets, and their prediction is that if the current rate of ice melt continues, sea levels could rise six inches by the year 2100.
rows.zh: 上周发表在《自然》杂志的一项新研究中，来自多个国家的80多位科学家，利用卫星数据研究了南极广袤的冰盖；他们预测，如果当前融冰速度持续下去，到2100年，海平面可能上升6英寸。

rows.en: Yesterday, for example, there were huge floods in some of the areas around the country, and these floods wouldn’t have happened without the sea level rise that we’ve already seen.
rows.zh: 比如，昨天全国一些地区发生了严重洪水；如果没有我们已经经历的海平面上升，这些洪水本来不会发生。

rows.en: Well, they have a lot of direct measurements from satellites of the height of the surface of the ice sheets, so they’re able to see how that height changes over time.
rows.zh: 他们有大量卫星对冰盖表面高度的直接测量数据，因此能看出这些高度如何随时间变化。

rows.en: Yeah. If we continue to see the ice melt speeding up, and don’t cut back on our climate pollution emissions, then we’re pointed more towards six feet, possibly, rather than the three feet predicted by 2100, and that will be unmanageable in very many places.
rows.zh: 是的。如果冰融化继续加速，而我们又不减少气候污染物的排放，那么到2100年，海平面上升可能会更接近6英尺，而不是预测的3英尺；这对许多地方来说将难以应对。

rows.en: So even if everyone stopped driving, all the factories shut down, and somehow we didn’t produce CO2, we’re still going to see the effects of climate change.
rows.zh: 所以，即使每个人都停止开车，所有工厂都关闭，而且我们设法不再产生二氧化碳，气候变化的影响仍会持续出现。
